mechanism.base: Your core is Fire, and Wood feeds Fire: dry branches make the flame. Everything gathered and grown, books read, friendships tended, skills stacked like cordwood, is the fuel your light actually burns. That is why Wood is your Mind, the intake that restores what shining spends. A fire is not kept alive by burning harder. It is kept alive by the woodpile.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the flame eats scraps: brilliance flaring on no reserves, warmth borrowed from tomorrow. Your chart asks you to stack wood. Learn, gather, befriend, store.
mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the woodpile buries the fire: fuel hoarded past burning, preparation stacked so high the flame never gets lit. Pull a branch off the pile and strike.

function.definition_catalyst: Wood is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is how your fuel accumulates: skills stacked, books finished, people learned from over years. What you gather quietly is what you later burn as brilliance. Keep one slow project that grows monthly, a course, a craft, a language, and refuse to rush it.
function.definition_friction: Wood is your Mind, and as a friction, it is gathering as a way of postponing: one more certification, one more plan, readiness that keeps moving its own finish line. You are prepared enough for the next real step. Book the thing you have been training for, this month, at whatever level you are.

dips.body: Green time restores the thinker: gardens, walks, and living things refill your fuel.

candidates.cta_verdict: Your mind gathers fuel long before it flares, and the ideas you feed patiently become the insights people call sudden.

__ore.retired_fn_body: The Root is your learning function: the seat where the world soaks in and becomes yours. With Wood running it, your mind absorbs like a canopy: reaching for new material, grafting idea onto idea until strange hybrids fruit. You learn by gathering and by growing, and every book, mentor, and friendship becomes future firelight. Keep planting. Your brilliance burns what your curiosity stacked.
